papers.full_text: Primary health care courseThe World Health Organization (WHO) has launched a new free online course to help strengthen understanding and implementation of primary health care (PHC). Available through the WHO Academy learning platform, The primary health care approach: a short course is designed to support health professionals, policy-makers and other stakeholders in applying PHC principles in practice.Although PHC has been a global priority for nearly 50 years, its implementation remains uneven and the concept is often misunderstood. The course addresses this gap through five modules covering the importance of PHC, its core components, strategies for strengthening PHC-oriented health systems and approaches to leading health system transformation.“A shared understanding of what PHC means and how it works can help us realize its full potential and turn this commitment into real improvements in people’s health and in how health systems perform,” said Kalipso Chalkidou, director of WHO’s department of Performance, Financing and Delivery.https://bit.ly/4xFJdVU Data on sexual violence against womenThe new technical brief Measuring non-partner sexual violence against women: data availability, methodological issues and recommendations for good practice is calling for more consistent and rigorous measurement of non-partner sexual violence against women and girls.An estimated 263 million women and girls aged 15 years and older, or 8% globally, have experienced sexual violence by someone other than an intimate partner at least once since the age of 15. However, the true scale of the problem is likely higher due to underreporting, stigma and significant gaps in available data.The brief highlights challenges in comparing data across countries because of differences in survey methods, definitions and populations included. It recommends greater standardization of measurement approaches, the use of behaviourally specific survey questions and stronger safeguards for ethical and confidential data collection.Improved data are essential to help governments and partners better understand the prevalence of non-partner sexual violence, strengthen prevention and response efforts, support survivors and monitor progress towards ending violence against women and girls.https://bit.ly/4jfA2HW Paediatric cancer medicines prequalificationWHO has issued its first-ever call for manufacturers of childhood cancer medicines to submit products for evaluation through the WHO Prequalification Programme. The initiative aims to expand access to quality-assured medicines for children with cancer, particularly in low- and middle-income countries, where survival rates remain below 30%, compared with more than 80% in many high-income settings.The expression of interest covers 12 essential childhood cancer medicines, including six priority medicines that require child-friendly formulations and six medicines affected by significant access and supply challenges. The selection was informed by global consultations led through the Global Accelerator for Paediatric Formulations (GAP-f) and the Global Platform for Access to Childhood Cancer Medicines.By opening a pathway for manufacturers to seek WHO prequalification, the initiative is expected to strengthen the availability of quality-assured medicines for procurement and support countries in improving cancer care for children.“The expression of interest demonstrates the value of an end-to-end approach to paediatric medicines,” said Martina Penazzato, GAP-f lead, WHO Science for Health department. “Through GAP-f, we have moved systematically from horizon scanning and drug optimization to target product profiles and now to a concrete regulatory pathway that can stimulate manufacturers to develop and submit the products children need.”https://bit.ly/4ApWIvo Eliminating dog-transmitted rabiesWHO has validated Bhutan and Chile for eliminating dog-transmitted rabies as a public health problem, marking important progress in the global effort to end human deaths from dog-mediated rabies by 2030. Bhutan is the first country in the WHO South-East Asia Region to receive the validation, while Chile's validation builds on decades of coordinated action across the Americas, which has made the region a global leader in eliminating dog-transmitted rabies.Rabies remains one of the world's deadliest neglected tropical diseases and is almost always fatal once symptoms appear. However, human cases can be prevented through mass dog vaccination, effective surveillance and timely access to post-exposure treatment. Globally, dog-transmitted rabies continues to claim tens of thousands of lives each year.The achievements of Bhutan and Chile reflect years of sustained investment in prevention and control measures. Chile has maintained more than five decades without a human rabies case transmitted by dogs, while Bhutan's success was built on a nationwide One Health approach linking human and animal health services, community engagement and dog vaccination programmes.The two validations demonstrate that dog-transmitted rabies can be eliminated through strong public health systems, cross-sector collaboration and long-term commitment to prevention and surveillancehttps://bit.ly/4xAf61S https://bit.ly/3SVecPx Pandemic agreement negotiationsWHO Member States have advanced negotiations on a proposed pathogen access and benefit-sharing (PABS) system, a key component of the WHO Pandemic Agreement designed to support a faster and more equitable response to future pandemics.The eighth meeting of the Intergovernmental Working Group on the WHO Pandemic Agreement brought together governments and stakeholders in Geneva to continue discussions on the PABS annex. The proposed system aims to facilitate the rapid sharing of pathogens with pandemic potential and related sequence information, while ensuring fair and equitable access to vaccines, therapeutics and diagnostics developed from their use.Finalizing the PABS annex is considered a critical step towards enabling countries to sign and consider ratification of the WHO Pandemic Agreement. Once completed, the agreement is expected to strengthen international cooperation, improve preparedness capacities and support a more coordinated response to future global health emergencies. https://bit.ly/4xxBCIZ New Science CouncilWHO has renewed its Science Council, appointing 21 leading scientists and experts from across disciplines, regions and generations to help guide the Organization on emerging scientific developments and innovations with implications for global health.The council includes specialists in public health, epidemiology, biomedical research, health systems, ageing, engineering, precision medicine and emerging technologies, with representation from all WHO regions as well as two Youth Council members. The inclusion of young scientists through the WHO Youth Council aims to ensure that future generations are represented in discussions on innovations that could shape global health in the decades ahead.“WHO is strengthening its ability to look ahead, identify transformative developments, and ensure that the benefits of scientific progress are translated into better health for people everywhere,” said WHO Director-General Tedros Adhanom Ghebreyesus. By providing independent scientific advice and strategic foresight, the Science Council supports WHO in identifying emerging health risks, opportunities and trends, helping to ensure that advances in science are translated into evidence-based policies and public health action worldwide.https://bit.ly/4y82Cj6 Tobacco use and infertilityTobacco smoking may be reducing the chances of conceiving for millions of people worldwide, according to a new knowledge summary from WHO. The publication highlights growing evidence that tobacco use can affect fertility in both women and men, while exposure to second-hand smoke may also increase reproductive risks. In addition, the publication emphasizes that tobacco use may reduce the success of fertility treatments, including in vitro fertilization, resulting in fewer pregnancies and live births.WHO recommends that health-care providers routinely inform individuals and couples planning a pregnancy about the reproductive risks of tobacco use and offer support to help them quit. Evidence on newer nicotine and tobacco products is still emerging, but WHO notes that these products may also pose risks to fertility and require further research.https://bit.ly/4yOPRKm Cover photoChildren queue to receive vaccines during an immunization campaign as part of the diphtheria outbreak response in the Banadir region of Somalia.WHO/Abdirahim Caaylaawe Looking ahead11–13 October. World Health Summit 2026. Berlin, Germany and online. https://bit.ly/3UUbHh1 19–22 October. Forty-ninth Expert Committee on Drug Dependence. Geneva, Switzerland. https://bit.ly/4rkKfVw 28–30 October. Meeting of the Malaria Policy Advisory Group. Online. https://bit.ly/478gQEN

papers.title_original: Public health round-up.

analysis.research_question_and_background: The study aimed to address the global challenge of rabies disease, particularly focusing on the prevention and control of dog-transmitted rabies, which remains a significant public health issue. The background highlights that rabies is one of the world's deadliest neglected tropical diseases and that human cases can be prevented through mass dog vaccination, effective surveillance and timely access to post-exposure treatment.
analysis.study_design_and_population: The study involved the validation of Bhutan and Chile for eliminating dog-transmitted rabies as a public health problem. These countries were recognized for their successful implementation of prevention and control measures, including nationwide One Health approaches, community engagement and dog vaccination programs.
analysis.methods: The methods included the evaluation of rabies prevention and control strategies, such as mass dog vaccination, effective surveillance systems and post-exposure treatment protocols. The study also considered the long-term commitment to these measures and cross-sector collaboration to achieve elimination.
analysis.main_results: The results indicate that Bhutan and Chile have successfully eliminated dog-transmitted rabies, with Chile maintaining over five decades without a human rabies case transmitted by dogs and Bhutan achieving this through a comprehensive One Health approach.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The authors interpret these findings as evidence that dog-transmitted rabies can be eliminated through strong public health systems, cross-sector collaboration and sustained prevention and surveillance efforts. This represents a novel demonstration of the feasibility of such elimination strategies in different contexts.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The findings can inform global efforts to eliminate rabies by highlighting the effectiveness of integrated public health strategies, particularly those involving mass dog vaccination and surveillance. They also provide a model for other countries to adopt similar approaches.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The evidence is based on reported achievements and does not include detailed statistical analysis or long-term follow-up data. However, the validation by WHO provides a high level of confidence in the effectiveness of the strategies employed in Bhutan and Chile.

analysis.summary_en: This paper discusses the validation of Bhutan and Chile for eliminating dog-transmitted rabies, highlighting the success of their public health strategies. It also covers other WHO initiatives, including a new course on primary health care, a technical brief on sexual violence against women, and the renewal of the Science Council. The paper emphasizes the importance of mass dog vaccination, surveillance, and post-exposure treatment in preventing rabies. The findings suggest that elimination is achievable through sustained efforts and cross-sector collaboration, offering valuable insights for global rabies control programs.

elements_zh.research_question_and_background: 该研究旨在应对 狂犬病 疾病的全球挑战,特别关注狗传播的 狂犬病 疾病的预防和控制,这仍然是一个重大的公共卫生问题。背景强调狂犬病是世界上最致命的被忽视的热带疾病之一,人类病例可以通过大量狗疫苗接种、有效的监测和及时获得暴露后的治疗来预防。
elements_zh.study_design_and_population: 该研究验证了不丹和智利消除狗传播的 狂犬病 公共卫生问题的能力。这些国家因其成功实施预防和控制措施而获得认可,包括全国范围内的“同一个健康”方法、社区参与和狗 疫苗接种 计划。
elements_zh.methods: 这些方法包括评估 狂犬病 预防和控制策略,例如群体犬 疫苗接种、有效的 监测 系统和暴露后 治疗 方案。该研究还考虑了对这些措施的长期承诺以及实现消除的跨部门合作。
elements_zh.main_results: 结果表明,不丹和智利已成功消除了狗传播的 狂犬病,智利在过去 50 年里一直没有出现狗传播的人类 狂犬病 病例,不丹则通过全面的“同一个健康”方法实现了这一目标。
elements_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 作者将这些发现解释为证据,表明狗传播的 狂犬病 可以通过强大的公共卫生系统、跨部门合作、持续的预防和 狂犬病 的努力来消除。这代表了此类消除策略在不同情况下的可行性的新颖证明。
elements_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 研究结果可以通过强调综合公共卫生策略的有效性,为全球消除 狂犬病 的努力提供信息,特别是那些涉及群体狗 疫苗接种 和 监测 的策略。它们还为其他国家采取类似方法提供了范例。
elements_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: 证据基于报告的成就,不包括详细的统计分析或长期随访数据。然而,世界卫生组织的验证对不丹和智利采用的策略的有效性提供了高度的信心。

analysis_zh.study_design_and_population: 该研究验证了不丹和智利消除狗传播的 狂犬病 公共卫生问题的能力。这些国家因其成功实施预防和控制措施而获得认可,包括全国范围内的“同一个健康”方法、社区参与和狗 疫苗接种 计划。
analysis_zh.methods: 这些方法包括评估 狂犬病 预防和控制策略,例如群体犬 疫苗接种、有效的 监测 系统和暴露后 治疗 方案。该研究还考虑了对这些措施的长期承诺以及实现消除的跨部门合作。
analysis_zh.main_results: 结果表明,不丹和智利已成功消除了狗传播的 狂犬病,智利在过去 50 年里一直没有出现狗传播的人类 狂犬病 病例,不丹则通过全面的“同一个健康”方法实现了这一目标。
analysis_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 作者将这些发现解释为证据,表明狗传播的 狂犬病 可以通过强大的公共卫生系统、跨部门合作、持续的预防和 狂犬病 的努力来消除。这代表了此类消除策略在不同情况下的可行性的新颖证明。

papers.title: Effectiveness Of a Structured Teaching Programme on Knowledge Regarding First Aid Management of Dog Bite Among Mothers: A Pre-Experimental Study
papers.abstract: Background: Dog bites constitute a significant public health problem, particularly among children, and are associated with physical trauma, wound infections, and the risk of fatal rabies transmission. Mothers, as primary caregivers, are pivotal in delivering immediate first aid; however, their knowledge regarding appropriate first aid management of dog bites is often inadequate. Structured teaching programmes (STPs) have demonstrated effectiveness in improving health-related knowledge in community settings. Objectives: To assess pre-test knowledge of mothers regarding first aid management of dog bite; to evaluate the effectiveness of an STP by comparing pre- and post-test scores; and to determine the association between pre-test knowledge and selected demographic variables. Methods: A pre-experimental one-group pre-test post-test design was employed. Fifty (N=50) mothers of children below 9 years residing in Aliparamba Panchayat Ward-4, Malappuram district, Kerala, were selected by non-probability convenience sampling. Data were collected using a self-developed structured knowledge questionnaire, whose content validity and reliability were established before data collection. A 30-minute STP incorporating pamphlets and demonstrations was delivered. Reliability and content validity were established through expert review and a pilot study. Descriptive statistics, paired t-test, and chi-square test were used for analysis. Results: Pre-test assessment revealed that 12% of mothers had poor knowledge, 78% had average knowledge, and 10% had good knowledge (mean 8.84, SD 2.38). Post-test findings showed a marked improvement: 76% of mothers achieved good knowledge and 24% average knowledge, with none remaining in the poor category (mean 15.72, SD 1.08). The mean difference was 6.88. The paired t-test yielded t(49)=19.47 (p 0.05). Conclusion: The STP significantly improved mothers' knowledge regarding first aid management of dog bites. Community-based educational interventions are recommended to empower caregivers, reduce complications, and mitigate rabies-related morbidity and mortality.

analysis.scope_and_question: The review focuses on the rabies virus and rabies disease. The central question is whether structured teaching programmes (STPs) can improve mothers' knowledge regarding first aid management of dog bites, which are a significant public health problem associated with rabies transmission.
analysis.evidence_base_and_review_method: The review is a pre-experimental study employing a one-group pre-test post-test design. Data were collected using a self-developed structured knowledge questionnaire, which was validated for content validity and reliability through expert review and a pilot study. The analysis included descriptive statistics, paired t-test, and chi-square test.
analysis.consensus_and_key_conclusions: The structured teaching programme significantly improved mothers' knowledge regarding first aid management of dog bites. Pre-test results indicated inadequate knowledge, with 12% of mothers having poor knowledge, while post-test results showed a marked improvement, with none remaining in the poor category. The mean difference in knowledge scores was 6.88, and the paired t-test was statistically significant (t(49)=19.47, p < 0.05).
analysis.controversies_and_evidence_gaps: The review does not report on controversies or evidence gaps related to the rabies virus or rabies disease. The study is limited to assessing knowledge improvement in a specific population and does not address broader biological or epidemiological aspects of rabies.
analysis.research_and_practice_implications: Community-based educational interventions are recommended to empower caregivers, reduce complications, and mitigate rabies-related morbidity and mortality. Further research is needed to evaluate the long-term impact of such programmes and their effectiveness in different populations and regions.

analysis.summary_en: This review evaluates the effectiveness of a structured teaching programme (STP) in improving mothers' knowledge about first aid management of dog bites, which are a significant public health concern linked to rabies transmission. The study employed a pre-experimental one-group pre-test post-test design, with data collected via a validated questionnaire. Results showed a substantial improvement in knowledge scores, with no mothers remaining in the poor knowledge category post-intervention. The mean difference was 6.88, and the paired t-test was statistically significant (t(49)=19.47, p < 0.05). The review concludes that such educational interventions are effective in enhancing caregivers' knowledge, potentially reducing rabies-related complications. However, it does not address broader biological or epidemiological aspects of rabies, highlighting a need for further research on the long-term impact and generalizability of these programmes.

papers.title: Frontline recognition and referral readiness for selected priority zoonoses among health workers in southwestern Uganda: a One Health systems assessment
papers.abstract: Abstract Background: Southwestern Uganda is a livestock-intensive region vulnerable to recurrent zoonotic disease outbreaks. Because confirmation of several priority zoonoses depends on higher-level or reference laboratories, preparedness requires both frontline recognition and effective specimen referral. We assessed recognition and referral readiness and related One Health implementation gaps among health workers in southwestern Uganda. Methods We conducted a cross-sectional survey among 345 health workers in Mbarara, Kazo, Kiruhura, and Ibanda districts. The study focused on Rift Valley fever (RVF), Crimean-Congo haemorrhagic fever (CCHF), Ebola, anthrax, and rabies. Participants were purposively recruited across facility levels based on frontline roles in recognition, specimen handling, referral, or reporting of suspected zoonoses. Recognition readiness was assessed using 11 disease-specific causative-agent and transmission/exposure items. Referral readiness was assessed using testing advice, specimen referral, result feedback, referral-to-result interval, and result communication. The primary outcome was a reported referral-linkage gap, defined as not reporting specimen referral elsewhere for testing. Modified Poisson regression with facility-clustered robust standard errors was used to estimate prevalence ratios. Results Almost all respondents had heard of the selected zoonoses (99.7%). Recognition was lower for RVF exposure through aborted fetuses or placentas (58.8%) and mosquito transmission (69.9%). Overall, 13.9% reported a referral-linkage gap, which was more common at lower-level facilities than at health centre IVs or hospitals (20.1% vs 6.8%; adjusted prevalence ratio [aPR]=2.74; 95% confidence interval [CI]=1.39–5.39; p =0.004). Among respondents reporting referral, 99.3% reported receiving results; the median referral-to-result interval was 10 days (IQR, 7–14). Commonly reported barriers were inadequate diagnostic resources (90.4%), unreliable transport (75.1%), and inadequate intersectoral collaboration (74.2%). Conclusions Frontline recognition of selected priority zoonoses was generally strong, but referral readiness was less consistent at lower levels of care. Strengthening peripheral specimen-referral connectivity, transport, information exchange, and One Health coordination should complement continued targeted disease-specific training.

elements_zh.research_question_and_background: 该研究旨在评估乌干达西南部卫生工作者对选定的优先人畜共患疾病的前线识别和转诊准备情况,因为该地区容易遭受复发性人畜共患疾病 暴发。
elements_zh.study_design_and_population: 对姆巴拉拉、卡佐、基鲁胡拉和伊班达地区的 345 名卫生工作者进行了一项横断面调查,这些卫生工作者是根据在识别、标本处理、转诊或报告疑似人畜共患病方面的一线角色而有目的地招募的。
elements_zh.methods: 使用 11 种疾病特异性病原体和 传播/暴露项目评估识别准备情况,同时通过测试建议、样本转诊、结果反馈、转诊到结果间隔和结果沟通来评估转诊准备情况。使用设施聚类稳健标准误差的修正泊松回归来估计 患病率 比率。
elements_zh.main_results: 几乎所有受访者都听说过所选的人畜共患病(99.7%)。主要结果是报告的转诊关联差距,定义为不报告样本转诊到其他地方进行检测,13.9% 的受访者报告了这一差距,这种差距在较低级别的设施中比在卫生中心静脉输液或医院更常见。
elements_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 作者得出的结论是,一线对选定的重点人畜共患病的认识普遍较强,但在较低水平的护理中,转诊准备情况不太一致,这凸显了改善连通性和协调的必要性。
elements_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 研究结果表明,加强外围标本转诊系统、运输、信息交换和 One Health 协调可以改善该地区人畜共患疾病 暴发 的准备情况。
elements_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: 该研究因其横截面设计和对自我报告数据的依赖而受到限制,这可能会引入偏差。由于这些限制,证据强度中等。

analysis_zh.research_question_and_background: 该研究旨在评估乌干达西南部卫生工作者对选定的优先人畜共患疾病的前线识别和转诊准备情况,因为该地区容易遭受复发性人畜共患疾病 暴发。
analysis_zh.study_design_and_population: 对姆巴拉拉、卡佐、基鲁胡拉和伊班达地区的 345 名卫生工作者进行了一项横断面调查,这些卫生工作者是根据在识别、标本处理、转诊或报告疑似人畜共患病方面的一线角色而有目的地招募的。
analysis_zh.methods: 使用 11 种疾病特异性病原体和 传播/暴露项目评估识别准备情况,同时通过测试建议、样本转诊、结果反馈、转诊到结果间隔和结果沟通来评估转诊准备情况。使用设施聚类稳健标准误差的修正泊松回归来估计 患病率 比率。
analysis_zh.main_results: 几乎所有受访者都听说过所选的人畜共患病(99.7%)。主要结果是报告的转诊关联差距,定义为不报告样本转诊到其他地方进行检测,13.9% 的受访者报告了这一差距,这种差距在较低级别的设施中比在卫生中心静脉输液或医院更常见。
analysis_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 作者得出的结论是,一线对选定的重点人畜共患病的认识普遍较强,但在较低水平的护理中,转诊准备情况不太一致,这凸显了改善连通性和协调的必要性。
analysis_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 研究结果表明,加强外围标本转诊系统、运输、信息交换和 One Health 协调可以改善该地区人畜共患疾病 暴发 的准备情况。
analysis_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: 该研究因其横截面设计和对自我报告数据的依赖而受到限制,这可能会引入偏差。由于这些限制,证据强度中等。

papers.title: Age-related patterns in delayed presentation and pre-hospital wound management for rabies post-exposure prophylaxis: a retrospective hospital-based study in Hangzhou, China, 2022–2025
papers.abstract: Abstract Background Timely rabies post-exposure prophylaxis (PEP) and appropriate wound care are essential after potential rabies exposure, and older adults may face barriers to both. This study described presentation timing and pre-hospital wound management in a hospital-based cohort in Hangzhou, China. Methods This retrospective cross-sectional study included 3327 exposure-related clinic presentations between October 2022 and October 2025 after exclusion of 7 system-test entries, 15 WHO Category I exposures, 13 confirmed continuation visits, 10 contradictory-date records and 2 unresolved duplicate records. Subsequent-calendar-day presentation was a date-based operational proxy for delay. Separate multivariable logistic models evaluated presentation timing and any pre-hospital wound self-treatment. Results 218/3327 (6.6%) exposure-related presentations occurred on a subsequent calendar day. The clinic-opening calendar period (October–December 2022) was associated with subsequent-calendar-day presentation (AOR 2.54, 95% CI 1.63–3.96; P < 0.001), as was pre-hospital wound self-treatment (AOR 2.72, 95% CI 2.00–3.69; P < 0.001). Patients aged ≥ 65 years had higher adjusted odds of subsequent-calendar-day presentation than those aged 15–44 years (AOR 2.28, 95% CI 1.31–3.96; P = 0.003). The estimate for any self-treatment in the ≥ 65-year group was lower but did not reach the conventional significance threshold (AOR 0.71, 95% CI 0.50–1.01; P = 0.056). Conclusions In this hospital-based cohort, older age was associated with subsequent-calendar-day presentation. The estimate for lower self-treatment among older adults was imprecise and requires confirmation; the two outcomes were modelled separately and do not establish a combined individual-level outcome. Associations with the clinic-opening calendar period should be interpreted as exploratory because they may reflect clinic establishment, case mix, seasonality, or unmeasured access factors. Trial registration Clinical trial number: Not applicable.

papers.title_zh: 狂犬病 延迟就诊和院前伤口处理的年龄相关模式 暴露后预防:2022-2025 年在中国杭州进行的一项回顾性医院研究
papers.source_body_en: Abstract Background Timely rabies post-exposure prophylaxis (PEP) and appropriate wound care are essential after potential rabies exposure, and older adults may face barriers to both. This study described presentation timing and pre-hospital wound management in a hospital-based cohort in Hangzhou, China. Methods This retrospective cross-sectional study included 3327 exposure-related clinic presentations between October 2022 and October 2025 after exclusion of 7 system-test entries, 15 WHO Category I exposures, 13 confirmed continuation visits, 10 contradictory-date records and 2 unresolved duplicate records. Subsequent-calendar-day presentation was a date-based operational proxy for delay. Separate multivariable logistic models evaluated presentation timing and any pre-hospital wound self-treatment. Results 218/3327 (6.6%) exposure-related presentations occurred on a subsequent calendar day. The clinic-opening calendar period (October–December 2022) was associated with subsequent-calendar-day presentation (AOR 2.54, 95% CI 1.63–3.96; P < 0.001), as was pre-hospital wound self-treatment (AOR 2.72, 95% CI 2.00–3.69; P < 0.001). Patients aged ≥ 65 years had higher adjusted odds of subsequent-calendar-day presentation than those aged 15–44 years (AOR 2.28, 95% CI 1.31–3.96; P = 0.003). The estimate for any self-treatment in the ≥ 65-year group was lower but did not reach the conventional significance threshold (AOR 0.71, 95% CI 0.50–1.01; P = 0.056). Conclusions In this hospital-based cohort, older age was associated with subsequent-calendar-day presentation. The estimate for lower self-treatment among older adults was imprecise and requires confirmation; the two outcomes were modelled separately and do not establish a combined individual-level outcome. Associations with the clinic-opening calendar period should be interpreted as exploratory because they may reflect clinic establishment, case mix, seasonality, or unmeasured access factors. Trial registration Clinical trial number: Not applicable.

analysis_zh.methods: 进行了一项回顾性横断面研究,使用单独的多变量逻辑模型评估就诊时间和任何院前伤口自我 治疗。
analysis_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 这些发现强调需要采取有针对性的干预措施来提高老年人的 狂犬病 PEP 依从性,特别是在诊所运营的早期。

papers.title: Immunoinformatic Design and Structural Evaluation of a Full-Length mRNA Vaccine Targeting Rabies Glycoprotein G
papers.abstract: Background/Objectives: Rabies remains a fatal viral disease, and current conventional vaccine strategies face significant challenges regarding structural stability and large-scale manufacturing. This study aimed to design a novel messenger ribonucleic acid (mRNA) vaccine candidate targeting the rabies virus glycoprotein G (RABV-G) using an integrated immunoinformatic and structural modeling framework. Methods: The RABV-G sequence was systematically evaluated for evolutionary conservation and safety, followed by 3D structural modeling. Highly antigenic B-cell and T-cell epitopes were identified based on human leukocyte antigen (HLA) binding, toxicity, and glycosylation shielding analyses. Functional interactions were assessed via molecular docking with the Toll-like Receptor 4/Myeloid Differentiation factor 2 (TLR4-MD2) complex. Finally, a full-length mRNA construct was engineered and computationally evaluated for translational efficiency, structural stability, and immune simulation. Results: The RABV-G target exhibited high evolutionary conservation, with 53.82% of positions fully identical and an additional 43.70% highly conserved (70–99%) across 87 analyzed sequences. Structural validation confirmed a high-quality model, enabling the extraction of accessible, non-glycosylated epitopes. Molecular docking simulations revealed a highly favorable predicted structural interaction with the TLR4-MD2 receptor, suggesting a potential structural capacity to engage innate immune pathways, pending experimental validation. The codon-optimized mRNA construct exhibited a predicted thermodynamically stable secondary structure (MFE = −429.50 kcal/mol) with an accessible translation initiation site, pending experimental validation. Furthermore, in silico immune simulations predicted a robust and sustained activation of both humoral and cellular immunity, notably including memory B-cell expansion. Conclusions: The computationally designed mRNA vaccine candidate demonstrates highly favorable structural characteristics and immunogenic potential. While these in silico findings present a promising foundational framework for rabies prevention, subsequent experimental laboratory validation is strictly required to confirm its functional efficacy and translation.

elements_zh.research_question_and_background: 狂犬病 仍然是一种致命的病毒性疾病,当前传统的 疫苗 策略在结构稳定性和大规模制造方面面临着重大挑战。本研究旨在使用集成的免疫信息学和结构建模框架设计一种针对 狂犬病病毒 糖蛋白 G (RABV-G) 的新型信使核糖核酸 (mRNA) 疫苗 候选物。
elements_zh.study_design_and_population: 该研究采用计算机模拟方法进行,重点关注 狂犬病病毒 糖蛋白 G (RABV-G) 及其结构和免疫原性特性。该研究涉及对 87 个 RABV-G 分析序列进行评估,以评估进化保守性和安全性。
elements_zh.methods: 对 RABV-G 序列的进化保守性和安全性进行了系统评估,然后进行 3D 结构建模。基于人类白细胞抗原 (HLA) 结合、毒性和糖基化屏蔽分析,鉴定了高抗原性 B 细胞和 T 细胞表位。通过与 Toll 样受体 4/骨髓分化因子 2 (TLR4-MD2) 复合物的分子对接来评估功能相互作用。设计了全长 mRNA 构建体,并通过计算评估了翻译效率、结构稳定性和免疫模拟。
elements_zh.main_results: RABV-G 靶标表现出高度的进化保守性,在 87 个分析序列中,53.82% 的位置完全相同,另外 43.70% 的位置高度保守 (70-99%)。结构验证证实了高质量模型,能够提取可接近的非糖基化表位。分子对接模拟揭示了与 TLR4-MD2 受体的高度有利的预测结构相互作用,表明其具有参与先天免疫途径的潜在结构能力,有待实验验证。密码子优化的 mRNA 构建体表现出预测的热力学稳定二级结构 (MFE = -429.50 kcal/mol) 和可访问的翻译起始位点,有待实验验证。
elements_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 计算设计的 mRNA 疫苗 候选物表现出非常有利的结构特征和免疫原性潜力。这些计算机研究结果为 狂犬病 预防提供了一个有前途的基础框架。
elements_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 这些发现为开发针对 狂犬病 的新 mRNA 疫苗 提供了有希望的基础,这可以提高结构稳定性和大规模生产。该结果可能为未来 疫苗 设计和免疫原性的研究提供信息。
elements_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: 该研究基于计算机分析,需要随后的实验实验室验证以确认功能功效和翻译。证据是温和的,因为它依赖于计算模型而不是经验数据。

analysis_zh.main_results: RABV-G 靶标表现出高度的进化保守性,在 87 个分析序列中,53.82% 的位置完全相同,另外 43.70% 的位置高度保守 (70-99%)。结构验证证实了高质量模型,能够提取可接近的非糖基化表位。分子对接模拟揭示了与 TLR4-MD2 受体的高度有利的预测结构相互作用,表明其具有参与先天免疫途径的潜在结构能力,有待实验验证。密码子优化的 mRNA 构建体表现出预测的热力学稳定二级结构 (MFE = -429.50 kcal/mol) 和可访问的翻译起始位点,有待实验验证。
analysis_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 计算设计的 mRNA 疫苗 候选物表现出非常有利的结构特征和免疫原性潜力。这些计算机研究结果为 狂犬病 预防提供了一个有前途的基础框架。
analysis_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 这些发现为开发针对 狂犬病 的新 mRNA 疫苗 提供了有希望的基础,这可以提高结构稳定性和大规模生产。该结果可能为未来 疫苗 设计和免疫原性的研究提供信息。
analysis_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: 该研究基于计算机分析,需要随后的实验实验室验证以确认功能功效和翻译。证据是温和的,因为它依赖于计算模型而不是经验数据。

papers.title: Rabies Prevention in Practice, Awareness, Immediate Bite Response, Care-Seeking, and Barriers among Grade 5 Pupils and Their Parents in a Selected Public Elementary School in San Pablo City, Laguna
papers.abstract: Rabies remains a critical public health concern in the Philippines, particularly among school-aged children who are at increased risk because of frequent contact with domestic and stray animals. This study assessed the awareness, immediate bite response, care-seeking behavior, and perceived barriers to rabies prevention among Grade 5 pupils and their parents in San Pablo City, Laguna. A descriptive, comparative, and cross-sectional research design was employed, involving 302 Grade 5 pupils and their corresponding parents. Data were gathered using a structured questionnaire that examined participants’ knowledge of rabies transmission, prevention practices, immediate wound management, care-seeking intentions, and barriers to treatment. Findings revealed that most participants demonstrated a high level of awareness regarding rabies, with 71.19% of pupils and 75.83% of parents recognizing dog bites as the primary mode of transmission. However, misconceptions persisted, particularly among pupils, regarding the possibility that apparently healthy animals could still transmit rabies. Although most respondents expressed a strong intention to seek medical care following an animal bite, with 90% of pupils and 85% of parents indicating they would visit a health facility, deficiencies remained in recommended first-aid practices, including proper wound washing and avoidance of traditional remedies. Financial constraints, reported by 60% of parents, fear of vaccination, and limited access to healthcare facilities were identified as the major barriers to timely treatment. The findings indicate that awareness alone is insufficient to ensure appropriate preventive behaviors. Strengthening school- and community-based health education, correcting misconceptions, improving access to affordable post-exposure prophylaxis, and promoting collaboration among healthcare providers, educational institutions, and local government units are essential to enhance rabies prevention and encourage timely responses to potential rabies exposure.
papers.journal: The International Review of Multidisciplinary Research

It highlights that while awareness of rabies transmission is generally high, misconceptions about healthy animals transmitting the disease persist. papers.title: Beneath the bark: mapping dog bite patterns and injury severity – a cross-sectional study at rural health training centre Santhpur, Bidar, Karnataka
papers.abstract: Background: Rabies is a vaccine-preventable, zoonotic, viral disease that invariably affects the central nervous system, with dogs responsible for virus transmission in up to 99% of human cases. India remains endemic for rabies and accounts for approximately 36% of global rabies deaths. Objectives were to describe the pattern and severity of injuries among patients presenting with dog bite complaints to rural health training centre. Methods: A prospective cross-sectional study was conducted from February 2026 to May 2026 at RHTC Santhpur, Bidar. All 63 patients presenting with dog bite complaints were enrolled and data were collected using a structured questionnaire covering socio-demographic profiles, bite characteristics, wound categorization, and post-exposure management. Analysis was performed using Microsoft Excel 2022. Results: Of the 63 patients, 46 (73%) were male. The most affected age group was 6-25 years (42.86%). The majority of bites occurred in the evening (38.1%) and stray dogs accounted for (52.4%) of bites. Unprovoked bites were predominant (77.78%). Lower limbs were the most commonly bitten site (71.4%). Category II wounds predominated (85.7%), while category III wounds constituted (14.3%). First aid with soap and water was performed by (98.4%) of victims. However, only (11.1%) of category III patients received rabies immunoglobulin (RIG). Conclusions: Dog bites predominantly affect young, productive-age males, with a near-equal burden from stray and pet dogs. The critical gap in RIG availability for category III patients represents a serious public health concern requiring urgent systemic intervention.
papers.journal: International Journal of Research in Medical Sciences

analysis.study_design_and_population: A prospective cross-sectional study was conducted from February 2026 to May 2026 at RHTC Santhpur, Bidar. analysis.summary_en: This study aimed to describe the pattern and severity of injuries among patients presenting with dog bite complaints at a rural health training centre in Bidar, Karnataka. Conducted from February to May 2026, it enrolled 63 patients and collected data on socio-demographic profiles, bite characteristics, wound categorization, and post-exposure management. The results showed that 73% of the patients were male, with the most affected age group being 6-25 years. Bites predominantly occurred in the evening, with stray dogs responsible for 52.4% of incidents. Unprovoked bites were common, and lower limbs were the most frequently bitten site. Category II wounds were most prevalent, while only 11.1% of category III patients received rabies immunoglobulin. The authors concluded that young males are most affected, and the lack of RIG availability for severe wounds is a significant public health issue. The study's findings are limited by its single-centre design and small sample size, which may affect generalizability.

elements_zh.research_question_and_background: 狂犬病 是一种 疫苗 可预防的人畜共患病毒性疾病,总是影响中枢神经系统,在高达 99% 的人类病例中,狗是 传播 病毒的传播者。印度仍然是 狂犬病 的流行病,约占全球 狂犬病 死亡人数的 36%。
elements_zh.study_design_and_population: 2026 年 2 月至 2026 年 5 月在 Bidar 的 RHTC Santhpur 进行了一项前瞻性横断面研究。所有 63 名有狗咬伤投诉的患者均被纳入研究,并使用结构化调查问卷收集数据,内容涵盖社会人口统计资料、咬伤特征、伤口分类和暴露后管理。
elements_zh.methods: 使用 Microsoft Excel 2022 进行分析。该研究旨在描述向农村卫生培训中心提出狗咬伤投诉的患者的受伤模式和严重程度。
elements_zh.main_results: 63 名患者中,46 名(73%)为男性。受影响最大的年龄组是6-25岁(42.86%)。大多数咬伤事件发生在晚上(38.1%),其中流浪狗咬伤事件占(52.4%)。无端咬伤占大多数(77.78%)。下肢是最常被咬伤的部位(71.4%)。II 类伤口占主导地位(85.7%),III 类伤口也占多数(14.3%)。(98.4%) 的受害者使用肥皂和水进行急救。然而,只有(11.1%)的 III 类患者接受了 狂犬病 免疫球蛋白(RIG)。
elements_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 狗咬伤主要影响年轻的生育年龄的男性,流浪狗和宠物狗的咬伤负担几乎相同。III 类患者 RIG 可用性的严重差距代表了一个严重的公共卫生问题,需要紧急系统干预。
elements_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 研究结果强调需要改进暴露后管理,特别是对于 III 类伤口,并强调解决农村地区 RIG 可用性的公共卫生问题的重要性。
elements_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: 该研究仅限于单个农村卫生培训中心,可能无法推广到其他地区。证据是中等的,因为它是基于样本量相对较小的横断面研究。

papers.title: A mixed-methods study of community dog management and rabies awareness in Thailand
papers.abstract: Rabies elimination requires coordinated interventions across the human-animal-environment interface, yet sustained progress is often hindered by systemic gaps between dog population management, community engagement, and governance. This study investigated community perceptions and challenges related to rabies prevention and control across high-endemic areas in Thailand. Using a mixed-methods design, secondary provincial quantitative data were integrated with qualitative thematic analysis from 57 stakeholders in high endemic areas, including public health officials, policymakers, NGOs, animal-welfare liaisons, and community members. The findings indicated standard rabies awareness, 98.2% of participants demonstrated good preventive practices, recognized post-exposure prophylaxis (PEP) as essential, and 68.4% possessed good knowledge. Although most supported dog sterilization (59.6%) and vaccination (63.2%), only 19.3% perceived existing control campaigns as effective. Main challenges included constrained operational resources (57.9%) and limited local government budgets (40.4%). Free-roaming community dogs were prevalent, with 54.4% of participants identifying abandonment as the primary driver of population growth. Informal feeding networks provided localized care for community dogs. While public willingness to fund management was relatively low (33.3% willing to pay; 19.3% supporting co-payment), reflecting an expectation of local authority responsibility. Qualitatively, unclear boundaries between public health mandates and animal welfare legal frameworks added complexity to rabies outbreak response and sometimes introduced institutional challenges among local government and non-governmental sectors. Nevertheless, stakeholders strongly supported sustained sterilization and intersectoral collaboration. Addressing policy-practice gaps, stabilizing financing, and integrating community social dynamics into formal One Health governance are crucial for achieving sustainable rabies elimination.

papers.title: Sheep-Associated Malignant Catarrhal Fever in an Exotic Rusa Deer (Cervus timorensis): Implications for Wildlife Health in Southern Brazil
papers.abstract: Sheep-associated malignant catarrhal fever (SA-MCF) is a frequently fatal, pantropic, lymphoproliferative disease caused by ovine gammaherpesvirus 2 (OvGHV2), with sheep serving as the asymptomatic reservoir host. Although the Rusa deer (Cervus timorensis) are known to be highly susceptible to OvGHV2 in other regions, cases have not been documented in this species from Brazil. This report describes the spontaneous occurrence of OvGHV2 infection in a captive Rusa deer from Southern Brazil and discusses possible impacts on wildlife. Three deer from the same property died suddenly without prior clinical signs. These animals had no known contact with sheep or goats, but were maintained in an epidemiological niche where OvGHV2 was detected in subclinically infected free-ranging wild boars (FRWBs) and cattle. One of these was submitted for routine post-mortem evaluations. Gross lesions included ulcerative and erosive lesions of the alimentary tract, pulmonary edema, and marked meningeal congestion. Histopathology revealed erosive and ulcerative esophagitis, abomasitis, omasitis, and rumenitis, with nonsuppurative meningoencephalitis, and vasculitis in several organs, consistent with SA-MCF. Molecular testing of brain tissue detected OvGHV2 DNA by qPCR. Furthermore, PCR assays amplified the partial fragments of the OvGHV2 tegument protein (ORF75) and the glycoprotein (gB) genes. Other neurological pathogens of ruminants including BoAHV5, BVDV, Listeria monocytogenes, Histophilus somni, and rabies virus were not detected. Additionally, phylogenetic analyses, based on ORF75 and gB genes, revealed that the nucleotide sequences derived from this study clustered with and had elevated sequence homology with the OvGHV2 reference strains and other strains derived from ruminants maintained in different geographical locations. The absence of contact with sheep, combined with prior evidence of subclinical OvGHV2 infection in FRWBs and cattle within the same epidemiological niche, suggests the involvement of alternative wildlife reservoirs or bridge hosts in viral transmission. Additionally, these results expand the host range of OvGHV2 in Brazil, highlight the vulnerability of exotic cervids to SA-MCF, and underscore the need for integrated wildlife–livestock surveillance strategies in regions where multiple susceptible species coexist.

papers.title: 5’ untranslated region (5’ UTR) of bovine β-globin in the mRNA constructs translates different types of antigenic proteins
papers.abstract: Synthetic messenger RNA (mRNA) is emerging as next generation vaccine platform. As natural 5’UTRs of particular genes do not work for other than its own mRNA, it is essential to identify an ideal 5’UTR supporting higher translation efficiency for different antigens. Six natural 5’UTRs derived from α, β-globin genes of host animals and other viral genes were cloned upstream to the coding sequences of reporter proteins. The corresponding capped mRNA were produced through in vitro transcription and the translation efficiency was assessed using flow cytometry, bioluminescence, immunofluorescence and western blot experiments. The results revealed higher translation of reporter proteins by bovine β-globin 5’UTR in different cell lines. Further, the chosen 5’UTR supported mRNA translation to produce different antigenic proteins such as rabies virus glycoprotein (RVG), major structural protein of foot and mouth disease virus (VP1) and bacterial epsilon toxoid protein (Eptx). Bovine -globin 5’UTR not only increased the translation efficiency of reporter proteins but also supported the expression of different antigenic proteins. Hence, bovine -globin 5’UTR can be used in the mRNA vaccine designs against animal diseases.

analysis.research_question_and_background: The study aimed to address the need for an ideal 5’UTR that supports higher translation efficiency for different antigens, as natural 5’UTRs of particular genes do not work for other than its own mRNA. This is critical for the development of next-generation mRNA vaccine platforms.
analysis.study_design_and_population: The study involved cloning six natural 5’UTRs from α, β-globin genes of host animals and other viral genes upstream to the coding sequences of reporter proteins. The translation efficiency was assessed in different cell lines.
analysis.methods: The corresponding capped mRNA were produced through in vitro transcription, and translation efficiency was evaluated using flow cytometry, bioluminescence, immunofluorescence and western blot experiments.
analysis.main_results: The results revealed that the bovine β-globin 5’UTR significantly increased the translation efficiency of reporter proteins across different cell lines. Additionally, it supported the expression of various antigenic proteins such as rabies virus glycoprotein (RVG), major structural protein of foot and mouth disease virus (VP1) and bacterial epsilon toxoid protein (Eptx).
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The authors interpreted these findings as evidence that the bovine β-globin 5’UTR can be effectively used in mRNA vaccine designs against animal diseases, highlighting its versatility in supporting translation of different antigenic proteins.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The findings can inform the development of more effective mRNA vaccines for animal diseases, particularly those targeting rabies virus and related pathogens, by providing a reliable 5’UTR that enhances translation efficiency.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study is limited to in vitro assessments and does not include in vivo validation, which may affect the generalizability of the findings. However, the results are supported by multiple experimental methods, providing moderate confidence in the effectiveness of the bovine β-globin 5’UTR.

analysis.summary_en: This study investigated the potential of the bovine β-globin 5’UTR as a universal mRNA translation enhancer for different antigens. The research aimed to address the challenge of finding an effective 5’UTR for mRNA vaccine development, as natural 5’UTRs are gene-specific. The study involved cloning six natural 5’UTRs upstream to reporter proteins and assessing their translation efficiency in vitro. Results showed that the bovine β-globin 5’UTR significantly enhanced translation across various cell lines and supported the expression of different antigenic proteins, including rabies virus glycoprotein (RVG), foot and mouth disease virus (VP1), and bacterial epsilon toxoid protein (Eptx). The authors interpreted these findings as evidence that the bovine β-globin 5’UTR could be used in mRNA vaccine designs against animal diseases. The study's in vitro nature limits its generalizability, but the results are supported by multiple experimental methods, providing moderate confidence in the effectiveness of the 5’UTR. These findings have implications for improving mRNA vaccine platforms for animal diseases, particularly rabies.

analysis_zh.research_question_and_background: 本研究旨在解决需要一种理想的5’UTR以支持不同抗原的更高翻译效率的问题,因为某些基因的天然5’UTR仅对其自身的mRNA有效。这对于下一代mRNA 疫苗平台的开发至关重要。
analysis_zh.study_design_and_population: 本研究涉及从宿主动物的α、β-珠蛋白基因以及其他病毒基因中克隆六个天然5’UTR,并将其连接到报告蛋白的编码序列上游。翻译效率在不同细胞系中进行了评估。
analysis_zh.methods: 通过体外转录生成相应的加帽mRNA,并使用流式细胞术、生物发光、免疫荧光和Western blot实验评估翻译效率。
analysis_zh.main_results: 结果表明,牛β-珠蛋白5’UTR显著提高了报告蛋白在不同细胞系中的翻译效率。此外,它还支持多种抗原蛋白的表达,如狂犬病病毒糖蛋白(RVG)、口蹄疫病毒的主要结构蛋白(VP1)以及细菌epsilon毒素蛋白(Eptx)。
analysis_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 作者将这些发现解释为牛β-珠蛋白5’UTR可以有效地用于针对动物疾病的mRNA 疫苗设计的证据,突出了其在支持不同抗原蛋白翻译方面的多功能性。
analysis_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 这些发现可以为开发更有效的针对动物疾病的mRNA 疫苗提供信息,特别是针对狂犬病病毒及相关病原体的疫苗,通过提供一种可靠的5’UTR来增强翻译效率。
analysis_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: 本研究仅限于体外评估,未包括体内验证,这可能会影响研究结果的普遍适用性。然而,结果得到了多种实验方法的支持,对牛β-珠蛋白5’UTR有效性的信心中等。

papers.title: Assessing Preparedness of Ghanaians for Future Infectious Disease Outbreaks: COVID-19 Experience
papers.abstract: The COVID-19 pandemic exposed preparedness gaps and reinforced the role of individual and household behaviours in preventing infectious disease transmission.This study assessed preparedness for future outbreaks among adults in Ghana, using lessons from the COVID-19 experience.A community-based cross-sectional mixed-method study was conducted among 1,307 adults in six districts across the Ashanti, Greater Accra, and Savannah regions, using purposive and cluster sampling.Data were collected with a semi-structured questionnaire covering sociodemographic characteristics, knowledge, attitudes, preventive practices, access to health services, and health information sources.Preparedness was measured using a composite knowledge, attitudes, and practices (KAP) score.Quantitative data were analysed using descriptive statistics, multivariate regression, and mediation analysis, while qualitative responses were examined using deductive thematic content analysis.Respondents demonstrated moderate preparedness, with preventive practices stronger than disease-specific knowledge.Reported behaviours included COVID-19 vaccination (70%), LLIN use among children (91%) and adults (87%), handwashing with soap and water (70%), rabies vaccination for dogs (94%), mask use and avoidance of sick people during outbreaks (60%), health facility visits when sick (75%) and keeping essential supplies for at least 72 hours (52%).Preparedness seemed associated with sex, residence, access to vaccines, LLINs and health facilities, and credible health information, which may have mediated socio-demographic influences.Persistent gaps included vaccine safety concerns, LLIN use, reporting of unusual health events, and access to hygiene facilities and preventive resources.Strengthening health literacy, trusted risk communication, community engagement, and equitable access to routine preventive services may improve preparedness for future infectious disease outbreaks.
papers.journal: Texila international journal of public health

papers.title: Clinical and Sociodemographic Profile of Animal Bite Cases: Prospective Observational Study in Eastern India
papers.abstract: Background: Animal bite injuries are a significant public health issue globally, with a high incidence, particularly in countries like India.Dog bites, primarily from stray dogs, account for the majority of cases.While infections are common, rabies remains the most serious and preventable complication.This study focuses on the epidemiology, management, and complications associated with animal bites in South 24 Parganas, West Bengal, India.Methods: A prospective observational study was conducted over 2 years (January 2022-December 2023) at a government health facility.All patients seeking postexposure prophylaxis for animal bites were included, excluding bites from unknown animals.Data were collected through a structured questionnaire, including demographic details, bite specifics, and clinical examination.Follow-up was done for 1 month to monitor adverse effects following immunization (AEFI).Data were analyzed using descriptive statistics.Results: A total of 2,888 patients were included, with 60% males and a predominant age-group of 21-30 years.Most bites were from peridomestic/ stray animals (63.85%), and 77.49% were unprovoked.The majority of bites were categorized as category III (53%), and the lower limb was the most commonly affected site.While 94.22% completed the antirabies vaccination (ARV) course, mild AEFIs, such as fever and delayed skin hypersensitivity, were observed in 1% of cases.Conclusion: Animal bites are a critical public health issue, with stray dogs being the main source.Adherence to vaccination protocols is crucial for preventing rabies, and mild side effects from ARVs are rare.Public awareness and adherence to national guidelines for management are essential to reduce the impact of these injuries.

analysis.research_question_and_background: Animal bite injuries are a significant public health issue globally, with a high incidence, particularly in countries like India. Rabies remains the most serious and preventable complication of these injuries.
analysis.study_design_and_population: A prospective observational study was conducted over 2 years (January 2022-December 2023) at a government health facility in South 24 Parganas, West Bengal, India. All patients seeking postexposure prophylaxis for animal bites were included, excluding bites from unknown animals. A total of 2,888 patients were included, with 60% males and a predominant age-group of 21-30 years.
analysis.methods: Data were collected through a structured questionnaire, including demographic details, bite specifics, and clinical examination. Follow-up was done for 1 month to monitor adverse effects following immunization (AEFI). Data were analyzed using descriptive statistics.
analysis.main_results: Most bites were from peridomestic/stray animals (63.85%), and 77.49% were unprovoked. The majority of bites were categorized as category III (53%), and the lower limb was the most commonly affected site. While 94.22% completed the antirabies vaccination (ARV) course, mild AEFIs, such as fever and delayed skin hypersensitivity, were observed in 1% of cases.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: Animal bites are a critical public health issue, with stray dogs being the main source. Adherence to vaccination protocols is crucial for preventing rabies, and mild side effects from ARVs are rare.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The findings highlight the importance of public awareness and adherence to national guidelines for the management of animal bites to reduce the impact of these injuries. They also emphasize the need for improved rabies prevention strategies in high-risk populations.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study is limited to a single government health facility in South 24 Parganas, West Bengal, India, which may affect generalisability. The evidence is descriptive and based on a single centre, so the confidence is moderate.

analysis.summary_en: This study investigates the clinical and sociodemographic profile of animal bite cases in South 24 Parganas, West Bengal, India, over a 2-year period. It highlights the high incidence of animal bites, particularly from stray dogs, and the predominance of unprovoked attacks. The majority of bites were categorized as category III, with the lower limb being the most commonly affected site. While 94.22% of patients completed the antirabies vaccination course, mild adverse effects following immunization were observed in 1% of cases. The study underscores the critical public health issue of animal bites and the importance of adherence to vaccination protocols to prevent rabies. It also emphasizes the need for public awareness and improved management strategies. The study's findings are based on data collected from a single government health facility, which may limit generalisability, and thus the evidence is considered moderate in strength.

papers.title: Insights into the scale, organisation, implementation and motivations behind dog culling in a rabies-endemic setting
papers.abstract: Culling is recognised as ineffective and potentially counterproductive for sustainable dog population management and rabies control, yet the practice persists in many countries. Empirical data on the scale, organisation, implementation and motivations behind culling remain sparse, limiting understanding of its persistence, and implications. Focusing on Tanzania, a rabies-endemic country where culling has been documented, this study uses a mixed-methods approach, combining two structured surveys (survey of occurrence, n = 51; survey of practice in districts reporting culling, n = 16) and in-depth interviews with district and field-based veterinary and livestock officers (n = 8). Culling was reported in 45% of surveyed districts (23/51). Culling events were reportedly led by veterinary departments, often with involvement of other sectors and communities, with officers also describing communities as carrying out some culling independently. Culling was motivated by complaints, requests and orders about the number of and harms attributed to free-roaming dogs. Roaming dogs were culled regardless of ownership, sterilisation and vaccination status, using methods inconsistent with humane killing standards. Extrapolating from the survey data, using a stochastic simulation, we estimate approximately 26,000 dogs (95% CI 20,000-33,000) are culled annually nationwide. Culling was difficult to reconcile with evidence-based international guidance on dog population management and rabies control, national animal welfare legislation, and One Health principles, underscoring the need to understand and address the factors sustaining it. Addressing culling will require engaging with the wider concerns motivating the practice, and with the sectors and communities involved.

analysis.summary_en: This study explores the continued use of culling in rabies-endemic Tanzania despite its ineffectiveness for sustainable dog population management. Using mixed methods, including surveys and interviews, the research finds that culling is reported in 45% of districts and estimates approximately 26,000 dogs are culled annually. These findings highlight a gap between current culling practices and evidence-based rabies control strategies, suggesting that addressing the motivations behind culling is essential for effective disease management. However, the study's reliance on self-reported data and extrapolation limits the confidence in its estimates, resulting in moderate evidence strength.

elements_zh.methods: 该研究采用混合方法设计,包括结构化调查和访谈,并采用随机模拟从调查数据推断年度扑杀估计。
elements_zh.main_results: 45% 的调查地区报告了扑杀行为 (23/51)。该研究还估计,全国每年约有 26,000 只狗(95% CI 20,000-33,000)被扑杀。
elements_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 研究结果表明,扑杀是由社区投诉和机构命令驱动的,并且无论 疫苗接种 或绝育状态如何,扑杀都会发生,这凸显了实践与基于证据的指南之间的脱节。
elements_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 结果强调需要使扑杀实践与科学和公共卫生原则保持一致,并表明理解和解决扑杀背后的动机对于有效的 狂犬病 控制至关重要。
elements_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: 该研究基于调查数据和外推法,这可能会引入偏差并限制扑杀估计的精度。由于依赖自我报告的数据并且缺乏直接的生物学或临床测量,证据的强度中等。

papers.title: Paleoepidemiología para la Arqueología del Paisaje: el caso de La Mancha Alta (Península Ibérica) en la Edad Media
papers.abstract: This study analyses the environmental conditions that favored the occurrence of diseases frequently documented during the Spanish Middle Ages, the eleventh and sixteenth centuries, such as rabies, ergotism, plague, and malaria. Because these diseases require specific environmental conditions to emerge and spread, they can be explored as indirect indicators of past climatic conditions. The results suggest that rabies and ergotism were more prevalent during the Medieval Warm Period, when environmental conditions favored their transmission. In contrast, plague and malaria became widespread during the fourteenth and fifteenth centuries, coinciding with the climatic shift toward the Little Ice Age known as the Late Medieval Climate Transition. These diseases had a significant impact on the populations of the study area and provide valuable evidence for palaeoenvironmental reconstruction. The observed relationships between disease occurrence and climatic conditions suggest that the Medieval Warm Period was characterized by warm and humid conditions, the Late Medieval Climate Transition by warm and dry conditions, and the onset of the Little Ice Age by cold and dry conditions.

papers.title: Faktor-Faktor Yang Berhubungan dengan Kejadian Ghpr di Pulau Timor: Kajian Literatur
papers.abstract: Rabies is an infectious disease that causes problems in the brain and nerves. This disease can be transmitted to humans through saliva or bites from animals that are already infected with rabies. Among the 26 provinces that are rabies-endemic in Indonesia, East Nusa Tenggara (NTT) is the most affected province. From January to July 2024, NTT recorded 16,180 cases of animal bites that could cause rabies and 27 deaths due to rabies. The purpose of this literature review is to study the risk factors and socio-cultural behaviors of rabies-transmitting animals that occur on Timor Island (Indonesia). This review uses scientific publications from 2024-2026. The search was conducted from April to September 2026. The combination of search keywords includes Rabies, GHPR, Timor Island, rabies in Timor Island, with the main source being Google Scholar. Data from the articles that were found then identified risk factors and social, cultural, and geographical aspects that affect rabies control efforts on Timor Island. The results showed that risk factors and social, cultural, and geographical aspects influence rabies control efforts on Timor Island. The conclusion is that GHPR cases occurring on Timor Island are caused by many factors such as the number of dog ownerships, provocative actions towards dogs, the number of dogs in the area, individual knowledge, age, maintenance practices, contact with HPR, HPR health checks, and HPR vaccination.

papers.source_body_en: Rabies is an infectious disease that causes problems in the brain and nerves. This disease can be transmitted to humans through saliva or bites from animals that are already infected with rabies. Among the 26 provinces that are rabies-endemic in Indonesia, East Nusa Tenggara (NTT) is the most affected province. From January to July 2024, NTT recorded 16,180 cases of animal bites that could cause rabies and 27 deaths due to rabies. The purpose of this literature review is to study the risk factors and socio-cultural behaviors of rabies-transmitting animals that occur on Timor Island (Indonesia). This review uses scientific publications from 2024-2026. The search was conducted from April to September 2026. The combination of search keywords includes Rabies, GHPR, Timor Island, rabies in Timor Island, with the main source being Google Scholar. Data from the articles that were found then identified risk factors and social, cultural, and geographical aspects that affect rabies control efforts on Timor Island. The results showed that risk factors and social, cultural, and geographical aspects influence rabies control efforts on Timor Island. The conclusion is that GHPR cases occurring on Timor Island are caused by many factors such as the number of dog ownerships, provocative actions towards dogs, the number of dogs in the area, individual knowledge, age, maintenance practices, contact with HPR, HPR health checks, and HPR vaccination.

Bioinformatics), Stevenage, UK; 2Independent Investigator, Biotechnology and Disease Research Group, Nigeria Received: July 20, 2026 | Revised: August 18, 2026 | Accepted: September 08, 2026 | Published online: September 28, 2026 *Correspondence to: Leo Nnamdi Ozurumba-Dwight, AHRO Center for Academic Research (Public Health & Clin. Single-cell Transcriptomics and Antibody Immunotherapy: A Potential Dual Strategy against Antimalarial Drug Resistance. Gene Expr 2026;25(4):e00028. DOI: https://doi.org/10.14218/GE.2026. 00028. Malaria remains a serious global health challenge, with 282 million cases and 610,000 deaths in 2024.1 Despite gains from artemisinin-based combination therapies, drug resistance remains a major challenge in malaria control efforts and elimination,2,3 with Egypt certified malaria-free by WHO in 2024.1 Notably, genetic mutations, epigenetic and transcriptional regulation contribute to antimalarial drug resistance.4 Key gene mutation- related resistance mechanisms include PfK13 mutations for artemisinin, PfCRT/PfMDR1 mutations for chloroquine, and PfDHFR/PfDHPS mutations for sulfadoxine-pyrimethamine.2,5 Antimalarial pipelines can face challenges as Plasmodium falciparum and related Plasmodium species may adapt through several forms of plasticity, such as stage-specific expression programs and epigenetic switching without gene mutations. Single-cell transcriptomics may help identify parasite evasion mechanisms and could inform future antibody immunotherapy strategies targeting parasite subpopulations and conserved epi- topes. In this conceptual framework, candidate antigens associated with drug-tolerant or persistent parasite states would require inde- pendent validation for surface exposure and antibody accessibility before antibody-based targeting. The proposed approach could potentially help suppress resistant clones and address potential mechanisms of escape associated with drug-resistance genes,6 par- ticularly if such validated targets are associated with drug-tolerant or persistent parasite subpopulations. This would not eliminate drug resistance but could potentially help mitigate its emergence by reducing the survival of such subpopulations under drug pres- sure. This proposed strategy may complement approaches tar- geting metabolic resistance pathways. Potential benefits could include reducing recrudescence and blocking transmission-specific stages. Broad-acting antimalarials can target multiple parasite life- cycle stages,7 while transcriptional and epigenetic plasticity may contribute to parasite survival under drug pressure.4 This dual approach could potentially help prolong drug lifespan and limit the emergence of resistance. Sustained epidemiological surveillance of parasite mutant antigen diversity is valuable to support this. A coordinated framework could combine single-cell RNA sequencing (scRNA-seq) to map transcriptional heterogeneity and identify stage-specific vulnerabilities with antibody immuno- therapy informed by these transcriptomic insights, as proposed here as a potential dual-front strategy. Molecular therapeutics for malaria may benefit from this approach. This Opinion outlines key concepts in the heterogeneity- resolving ability of single-cell transcriptomics, linking these insights to guided antibody immunotherapy, and proposes their integration into an intervention that represents a novel conceptual framework for future therapeutic strategies against antimalarial drug resistance. Stage-specific transcription programs may vary across mero- zoite invasion, intraerythrocytic growth, and gametocyte transmission.8 This approach considers transcriptional states, not just proteins or static mutations, and is conceptually intended to help identify vulnerabilities relevant to resistance.4 Single-cell transcriptomics can help resolve this heterogeneity. By profiling individual parasite cells using single-cell transcriptomics across the parasite life cycle, researchers can identify which gene expres- sion programs are active under drug pressure.4 Recent scRNA-seq datasets reveal stage-specific gene expression patterns across the Plasmodium life cycle.8 This includes bifunctional PfDHFR-TS (gene ID Pf3D7_0417200), which is critical for folate and nucle- otide biosynthesis and has been identified in a sexual-stage scRNA-seq dataset.9 Other targets include Pf3D7_0316800, a 40S ribosomal protein S15A involved in protein synthesis.9 These are cell-level expression patterns that may be obscured in bulk RNA- seq.10 Antibodies are part of humoral immunity and synergize with cellular immunity. Monoclonal antibodies and nanobodies, the latter being ultrasmall antibody fragments with high stability and strong binding affinity, have been explored for malaria prevention. Most malaria monoclonal antibodies are designed to prevent infection rather than overcome established drug resistance. Pro- phylactic or preventive antibody immunotherapy (passive immun- oprophylaxis) is given before infection or before symptoms Gene Expr Ozurumba-Dwight L.N.: Transcriptomics and Ab therapy dual strategy 2 DOI: 10.14218/GE.2026.00028 | Volume 25 Issue 4, October 2026 Fig. 1. Mechanistic synergistic streams of ML/AI variants predictive power-aided single cell transcriptomics and antibody immunotherapy at host- parasite interface to tackle Plasmodium drug resistance. AI, artificial intelligence; ML, machine learning; RBC, red blood cell. develop to reduce the risk of infection or disease. Separately, the malaria vaccines RTS, S/AS01 and R21/Matrix-M were recom- mended by WHO in October 2021 and October 2023, respectively.11 Therapeutic or curative antibody therapy (passive immuno- therapy) is given after infection or after symptom onset to treat established infection. Antibody therapies may be used for either prevention or treatment, and both applications involve distinct clinical goals. Examples include monoclonal antibody therapy for Ebola and the use of rabies immunoglobulin for rabies.12,13 For malaria, monoclonal antibodies such as CIS43LS are under clin- ical investigation primarily as prophylactic interventions rather than as treatments for established infection.14 While single-cell transcriptomics is a discovery tool, when used in infectious disease research, it may help identify stage-specific expression states and candidate antigens that could inform antibody studies, while structural analyses can characterize determinants of antibody binding and genomic analyses can identify potential escape variants emerging during persistent infection (Fig. 1).15,16 Related genomic approaches have also been used to investigate viral variants associated with antibody escape in infectious diseases such as COVID-19. Transcriptomic maps may guide the discovery of future small- molecule targets. For instance, M5717, a Plasmodium eukaryotic translation elongation factor 2 inhibitor evaluated as a small- molecule antimalarial, has shown preclinical evidence of parasite clearance when combined with pyronaridine.17 Its identification is not attributed to single-cell transcriptomics. This distinction clari- fies that single-cell transcriptomics may help prioritize translation- related vulnerabilities, while other approaches are required to develop and deliver corresponding interventions. Mutations in pathogen proteins can confer antibody resistance when they result in reduced susceptibility to the parental antibody. Selecting for such mutants resistant to the particular parent antibody in cell culture is an established approach for studying antibody resistance,18 while antibody-driven escape variants have also been observed during persistent infection.16 Therefore, designing antibodies to target such proteins could, in principle, support the development of more escape-resistant thera- peutic antibodies. The central concept proposed here is that anti- body strategies might be combined with single-cell transcrip- tomics mapping of candidate proteins and variants to reduce the potential for parasite escape. This could represent a future thera- peutic strategy, but it requires experimental and clinical validation. Conventional drug pipelines have not failed; they have adapted and continue to deliver. Artemisinin combination therapy and emerging combinations such as ganaplacide-lumefantrine remain essential. Single-cell transcriptomics complements rather than replaces these approaches by adding resolution to parasite tran- scriptional plasticity that may be associated with tolerance and transmission. Future antibodies tailored to validated parasite anti- gens could potentially contribute to parasite inhibition, pending further validation.19 Barriers that block translation to human health include cost and access. Protection from some monoclonal antibodies can last for months,14 However, dosing, delivery, data integration challenges, the complexity of translating transcriptomic signatures into clinic- ally actionable therapeutic targets, and affordability may limit their use in low-income countries where the burden is highest.20 Single-cell transcriptomic analyses may also be affected by sampling and cell-recovery biases, which can influence the apparent representation of parasite stages and transcriptional states. Key proteins highlighted by single-cell transcriptomic studies require independent experimental, pharmacological, and clinical validation before they can be considered druggable targets. Addressing these challenges will require human-focused optimiza- tion, such as the application of optimized dose regimens, delivery Ozurumba-Dwight L.N.: Transcriptomics and Ab therapy dual strategy Gene Expr DOI: 10.14218/GE.2026.00028 | Volume 25 Issue 4, October 2026 3 routes, and formulations informed by human pharmacokinetics. Single-cell transcriptomics is a discovery and profiling method, not itself a treatment. Its power lies in decoding stage-specific transcription and cellular heterogeneity in Plasmodium parasites and identifying relevant states and candidates. Nanobodies could be considered “precision antibodies” when their targets are selected using identified variant information from single-cell transcriptomics. Transcriptomics could be used to identify antigens highly expressed during vulnerable stages or in drug-resistant subpopulations. Generally, future antibodies could be bioengineered using target-selection strategies informed by large single-cell transcriptomic datasets, together with predictive tools such as machine learning and artificial intelligence to identify antigens or molecular targets with a high likelihood of developing resistance-associated alterations. Such approaches could better guide the selection and use of appropriate neutralizing antibodies before resistance emerges (Fig. 1). Single-cell transcriptomics decodes stage-specific gene expression, transcriptional heterogeneity, and parasite adaptation. Antibody immunotherapy informed by such transcriptomic maps could support more precise interventions. Genetic mutations (such as PfK13, PfCRT, PfMDR1, PfDHFR, and PfDHPS) remain central to resistance, while transcriptional adaptation may provide additional layers of regulation that single-cell transcriptomics may help illuminate. Single-cell transcriptomics may help identify parasite-stage vulnerabilities and guide future target discovery, while antibody-based prevention and other precision interventions require further validation for affordability, delivery, durability, and clinical impact. Single-cell Transcriptomics and Antibody Immunotherapy: A Potential Dual Strategy against Antimalarial Drug Resistance. Gene Expr 2026;25(4):e00028. DOI: https://doi.org/10.14218/GE.2026. 00028. Malaria remains a serious global health challenge, with 282 million cases and 610,000 deaths in 2024.1 Despite gains from artemisinin-based combination therapies, drug resistance remains a major challenge in malaria control efforts and elimination,2,3 with Egypt certified malaria-free by WHO in 2024.1 Notably, genetic mutations, epigenetic and transcriptional regulation contribute to antimalarial drug resistance.4 Key gene mutation- related resistance mechanisms include PfK13 mutations for artemisinin, PfCRT/PfMDR1 mutations for chloroquine, and PfDHFR/PfDHPS mutations for sulfadoxine-pyrimethamine.2,5 Antimalarial pipelines can face challenges as Plasmodium falciparum and related Plasmodium species may adapt through several forms of plasticity, such as stage-specific expression programs and epigenetic switching without gene mutations. Single-cell transcriptomics may help identify parasite evasion mechanisms and could inform future antibody immunotherapy strategies targeting parasite subpopulations and conserved epi- topes. In this conceptual framework, candidate antigens associated with drug-tolerant or persistent parasite states would require inde- pendent validation for surface exposure and antibody accessibility before antibody-based targeting. The proposed approach could potentially help suppress resistant clones and address potential mechanisms of escape associated with drug-resistance genes,6 par- ticularly if such validated targets are associated with drug-tolerant or persistent parasite subpopulations. This would not eliminate drug resistance but could potentially help mitigate its emergence by reducing the survival of such subpopulations under drug pres- sure. This proposed strategy may complement approaches tar- geting metabolic resistance pathways. Potential benefits could include reducing recrudescence and blocking transmission-specific stages. Broad-acting antimalarials can target multiple parasite life- cycle stages,7 while transcriptional and epigenetic plasticity may contribute to parasite survival under drug pressure.4 This dual approach could potentially help prolong drug lifespan and limit the emergence of resistance. Sustained epidemiological surveillance of parasite mutant antigen diversity is valuable to support this. A coordinated framework could combine single-cell RNA sequencing (scRNA-seq) to map transcriptional heterogeneity and identify stage-specific vulnerabilities with antibody immuno- therapy informed by these transcriptomic insights, as proposed here as a potential dual-front strategy. Molecular therapeutics for malaria may benefit from this approach. This Opinion outlines key concepts in the heterogeneity- resolving ability of single-cell transcriptomics, linking these insights to guided antibody immunotherapy, and proposes their integration into an intervention that represents a novel conceptual framework for future therapeutic strategies against antimalarial drug resistance. Stage-specific transcription programs may vary across mero- zoite invasion, intraerythrocytic growth, and gametocyte transmission.8 This approach considers transcriptional states, not just proteins or static mutations, and is conceptually intended to help identify vulnerabilities relevant to resistance.4 Single-cell transcriptomics can help resolve this heterogeneity. By profiling individual parasite cells using single-cell transcriptomics across the parasite life cycle, researchers can identify which gene expres- sion programs are active under drug pressure.4 Recent scRNA-seq datasets reveal stage-specific gene expression patterns across the Plasmodium life cycle.8 This includes bifunctional PfDHFR-TS (gene ID Pf3D7_0417200), which is critical for folate and nucle- otide biosynthesis and has been identified in a sexual-stage scRNA-seq dataset.9 Other targets include Pf3D7_0316800, a 40S ribosomal protein S15A involved in protein synthesis.9 These are cell-level expression patterns that may be obscured in bulk RNA- seq.10 Antibodies are part of humoral immunity and synergize with cellular immunity. Monoclonal antibodies and nanobodies, the latter being ultrasmall antibody fragments with high stability and strong binding affinity, have been explored for malaria prevention. Most malaria monoclonal antibodies are designed to prevent infection rather than overcome established drug resistance.
